chunks: No eyes can penetrate Him, but He penetrates all eyes, and He is the Subtle, the All-Knowing.

key_terms.الْأَبْصَارُ: eyes (plural of basar, referring to the faculty of sight)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is 'beyond the grasp of eyes' yet 'penetrates all eyes'?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is often cited to support the doctrine of God's transcendence (tanzih) from physical dimensions and spatial limitations, distinguishing His essence from created beings. The attribute of 'Al-Latif' (The Subtle) highlights His ability to perceive all things with minute precision without being perceived by them, while 'Al-Khabir' underscores His exhaustive knowledge of inner realities. This duality reinforces the belief that while God is unseen, He is ever-present and aware of every detail of creation.
